passage: I'm Avni, and I want to tell this properly because it can happen to anyone. One morning my friend Sana showed me her phone. Private messages I'd sent Kashish while we were together, things I'd never said to anyone else, had been forwarded around half of class eleven, now that we had broken up. My face went numb. I felt sick and thought everyone was staring. For about a day I believed it was my fault for trusting him. It wasn't. Sharing what I sent in trust is a violation, and it is not mine to carry. I took screenshots before anything disappeared, and I didn't reply to anyone. Sana came with me to my mother, and then to the principal. The school called the police cyber cell with us. It was still awful, but I wasn't alone, and the counsellor sees me every week now.

qa.q: Who showed Avni the forwarded messages?
qa.a: Sana, Avni's friend, showed them on her own phone.

qa.q: What did Avni feel and believe at first?
qa.a: Sick, numb and ashamed. Avni thought everyone was staring, and for about a day believed it was Avni's own fault for trusting Kashish.

qa.q: What steps did Avni take that helped?
qa.a: Avni saved screenshots, did not reply to anyone, told Avni's mother and the principal with Sana there, joined the school's report to the cyber cell, and now sees the counsellor.

qa.q: How might Sana have seen the moment she showed the phone?
qa.a: Probably worried and caring. Sana chose to tell Avni and later went along to Avni's mother, which suggests she wanted to support Avni. 🤍

grounding: Avni's private messages were shared to shame Avni, who saves evidence, tells trusted adults, reports to school and the cyber cell, and seeks support.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 11C, Wednesday
During the first period, Samir's friend Yusuf asked to speak to me privately. He said private messages Samir had sent to his ex, Rehana, had been posted in a class group chat overnight, with mocking comments. Samir was in the washroom and wouldn't come out.
I went to him at once. He was shaking. I told him clearly that what was done to him is serious and wrong, and in no way his fault.
With his permission, Yusuf and I saved screenshots of the posts, the group name and times, before anything was deleted. I informed the principal before second period. Samir chose to call his father from my office; his father arrived within the hour.
The principal has contacted Rehana's parents and the group admin. Samir's father plans to file a complaint with the police cyber cell tomorrow. I have asked the counsellor to meet Samir this afternoon, and I will check on him before he leaves today.

qa.q: Who told the teacher about the posted messages?
How was Samir feeling when the teacher found him?
qa.a: He was shaking, clearly humiliated and frightened after his private messages were shared.

qa.q: What steps made the teacher's response wise?
qa.a: Telling Samir it wasn't his fault, saving evidence, informing the principal and Samir's father the same morning, and arranging counselling.

qa.q: How might Yusuf feel after reporting it?
qa.a: Yusuf probably feels worried for Samir but relieved that a trusted adult is acting quickly.

grounding: A teacher responds when a teen's private messages are shared to shame him: evidence saved, adults told, report and support arranged.

passage:
Thursday
I don't even know how to write this. Hafsa, my ex, sent screenshots of our private messages to her friends. The ones where I said I get nervous before exams and cried after Nana died. Now they're in a group of thirty people. Someone added laughing faces.
I wanted to disappear. I thought about not going back to school, ever.
But I remembered what the cyber-safety talk said: save everything first. So I took screenshots of the group, the names, the times.
Then I told Papa when he got home. He read everything, sat down next to me and said, "Chaitanya, this is not your fault. What she did is wrong, and serious." He wrote to the principal tonight. Tomorrow we're going to school together, and on Saturday we'll go to the police cyber cell to file a complaint.
I still feel sick. But I'm not holding it alone.

qa.q: How many people were in the group with the screenshots?
What was Chaitanya feeling after the messages were shared?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt humiliated and sick, wanting to disappear and never go back to school.

qa.q: Which steps did Chaitanya and Papa take, and why do they matter?
qa.a: Saving evidence, telling Papa the same day, emailing the principal, and planning a cyber cell complaint mean adults can act and Chaitanya isn't alone.

qa.q: How does Papa respond when he reads the messages?
qa.a: Papa sits beside Chaitanya, says clearly it isn't Chaitanya's fault and that the sharing was wrong and serious, and acts that same night.

grounding: A teen whose private messages were shared to shame them saves evidence, tells a parent the same day and plans to report it.
